title: Приглашение на кофе и падение на роликах  (Coffee Invitation and Rollerblade Fall)

segments.t: Thinking Denis is in love with bartender Sveta, Nikita persuades Sveta to meet Denis for coffee in an hour; meanwhile in the park, Lyova's rollerblading plan takes a painful tumble.
Слушай, Света, ты же знаешь, что ты нравишься одному человеку?
Не знаю, например, выпить с ним чашечку кофе через час.
Да я не устала, а ты самый лучший тренер.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Слушай, Света, ты же знаешь, что ты нравишься одному человеку?
'Listen, Sveta, you know that a certain person likes you, right?' Nikita raises the pitch on 'person' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Sveta answers right away.
'Suppose I know.' Sveta brings out the contrast between 'suppose so' and 'know' in a few short words.
'By the way, he is really suffering.' Nikita anchors the line on 'between', while 'suffers' completes the thought.
'And what should I do?' Sveta raises the pitch on 'to do' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question. Nikita answers right away.
Не знаю, например, выпить с ним чашечку кофе через час.
'I do not know, for example, drink a cup of coffee with him in an hour.' Nikita brings out the contrast between 'not' and 'know' in a few short words.
'Well alright, it is a deal.' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'agreed' covers a group or the polite 'you'.
'Let's rest a little.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'come on' and finishing on 'let us rest'. Sveta answers right away.
Да я не устала, а ты самый лучший тренер.
'Why, I am not tired, and you are the very best coach.' Sveta anchors the line on 'yes', while 'coach' completes the thought.
'On the other hand, I am very tired, sorry.' The grammar packs 'on the other hand' and 'sorry' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
'Lyova, be more careful!' Sveta brings out the contrast between 'Lyova' and 'more carefully' in a few short words.
'More carefully, watch where you are going!' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'more carefully' before landing on 'are driving'.
'Oh, help!' The meaning hinges on 'oh' working together with 'help' in spoken Russian. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
Слушай, Света, ты же знаешь, что ты нравишься одному человеку?
Не знаю, например, выпить с ним чашечку кофе через час.
Да я не устала, а ты самый лучший тренер.
Lyova goes flying off the park path into the bushes, only to spot someone even more dangerous approaching: his mother. See you in the next scene.
